review_evidence: TensorLib/Npy.lean defines NumPy byte order/dtype/header/ndarray structures and parsing/saving operations; TensorLib/Tensor.lean, Shape.lean, Index.lean, Broadcast.lean, and Ufunc.lean define the tensor representation and operations.
TensorLib/ByteArray.lean proves replicateSize and zerosSize; TensorLib/Dtype.lean proves losslessAntiSymmetric; TensorLib/Slice.lean proves stop/default/step direction and nonzero-step invariants.
The project has 19 primary Lean files and 26 proposition declarations across core modules rather than a test-only proposition surface, so it carries reusable checked formal interfaces and invariants.
summary: Retain TensorLib because it defines a substantial executable tensor data model together with checked invariants for byte arrays, dtypes, slicing, and related operations used by formal compiler/semantics projects.
